name: RegelSpraak in Markdown
comment: Colours ```regelspraak fenced blocks inside Markdown. Hand-written, unlike syntaxes/regelspraak.tmLanguage.json, which is generated from the language's ANTLR lexer: nothing here derives from the lexer, it only recognises the fence and hands its contents to source.regelspraak. Injected into text.html.markdown by the grammars contribution in package.json.

regelspraak-codeblock.comment: The fence pattern is character-for-character the one Markdown's own grammar uses for every other language, with the language names swapped: \G anchors to the tokenizer's position, group 2 remembers the opening indentation and group 3 the exact fence, and the trailing group takes an info string the way documentation tooling writes it (```regelspraak{1,3}). Deliberately not improved on — see the note on the inner rule. `rgs` is accepted beside the language id because that is the file extension.
regelspraak-codeblock.name: markup.fenced_code.block.markdown

patterns.comment: The `while` clause pops this content rule at any line that is nothing but a fence, but it does not end the block: the outer `end` above decides that, and it needs a fence as long as the opening one. So a shorter fence nested inside a longer block keeps its own line uncoloured and the lines after it stay RegelSpraak, which is what CommonMark says. An unclosed fence colours on until a fence of the same length or the end of the document — the behaviour of every built-in language block, and not worth diverging from.
